= SaintapediaFeedback =

Readers can suggest improvements from the floating '''Improve this article''' button on main-namespace pages. Editors triage that feedback at [[Special:SaintapediaFeedback]].

This page is the operator cheat-sheet: who can see what, which <code>MediaWiki:</code> pages exist, and what belongs in LocalSettings instead. It lives in the Project namespace so the widget (default namespaces: main only) does not appear on it, and so it stays out of article search / Special:AllPages / random article.

== For readers ==

* The widget is on main-namespace articles. Hide it for this tab with × or a long-press; restore from the screen-edge tab or '''Tools → Improve this article'''.
* Submissions are anonymous by default (public mode). hCaptcha and a per-IP rate limit apply.
* Public resolutions (curated summaries, not raw comments) live at <code>Special:SaintapediaFeedback/resolutions/&lt;pageid&gt;</code>.

== For editors ==

Dashboard: [[Special:SaintapediaFeedback]] (or Toolbox → '''Page feedback''' on an article).

{| class="wikitable"
! Right
! Default
! What it does
|-
| <code>saintapediafeedback-view</code>
| sysop
| Open the dashboard, process rows, bulk-action. Also granted by <code>$wgSaintapediaFeedbackAccessGroups</code> (LocalSettings.php).
|-
| <code>saintapediafeedback-viewemail</code>
| sysop
| See the optional contact-email field. Independent of dashboard access. <code>$wgSaintapediaFeedbackEmailAccessGroups</code> (LocalSettings.php) — '''can never be set to public/everyone''', regardless of configuration.
|-
| <code>saintapediafeedback-export</code>
| sysop
| Download JSON export. Independent of dashboard access. <code>$wgSaintapediaFeedbackExportAccessGroups</code> (LocalSettings.php)
|}

A block revokes dashboard access immediately, even for sysop.

'''Locking email or export to nobody''' takes two steps: revoke the sysop right in LocalSettings '''and''' set the matching <code>*AccessGroups</code> array to a dummy token such as <code>['no-one']</code>. An empty/unset array is not "nobody" — it falls back to sysop.

== Security settings (LocalSettings.php only) ==

Access, email-access, export-access, the rate limit, and CAPTCHA-required are '''not''' configurable from a wiki page (2026-09-10 review, F-08): editing a <code>MediaWiki:</code> page needs only <code>editinterface</code>, with no deploy or code review, which is too low a bar for anti-abuse and access controls. Set these directly:

<pre>
$wgSaintapediaFeedbackAccessGroups = [ 'sysop' ];        // or [ 'user' ] for any named account
$wgSaintapediaFeedbackEmailAccessGroups = [ 'sysop' ];    // '*' is always ignored here
$wgSaintapediaFeedbackExportAccessGroups = [ 'sysop' ];
$wgSaintapediaFeedbackRateLimit = 5;                      // public mode, per hashed IP per day
$wgSaintapediaFeedbackEnterpriseRateLimit = 50;           // enterprise mode
$wgSaintapediaFeedbackRequireCaptcha = null;              // null = auto from mode; true/false to force
</pre>

<code>0</code> as a rate limit '''rejects every submit''' — it is not "unlimited".

== On-wiki config pages (operational knobs only) ==

These three remain overridable from a <code>MediaWiki:</code> page (<code>editinterface</code> only) because they are operational preferences, not security controls. One value per line; <code>#</code> comments, blank lines, and a leading wiki-list <code>*</code> are ignored. Save/delete/move invalidates the cache immediately (no hour wait). '''If a page is missing or empty, LocalSettings / PHP defaults apply.'''

{| class="wikitable"
! Page
! Format
! Default when empty
! On a cache/DB read failure
|-
| [[MediaWiki:SaintapediaFeedback-notify-users]]
| one username per line
| LocalSettings list
| PHP value. Log: <code>using PHP value</code>
|-
| [[MediaWiki:SaintapediaFeedback-show-public-counts]]
| <code>true</code> / <code>false</code>
| off
| PHP value. Log: <code>using PHP value</code>
|-
| [[MediaWiki:SaintapediaFeedback-enable-talklink]]
| <code>true</code> / <code>false</code>
| on
| PHP value. Log: <code>using PHP value</code>
|}

Do '''not''' put the hCaptcha secret or the LLM webhook token on a MediaWiki page. Those pages are world-readable.

== PHP warnings to grep ==

During an overlay read failure on one of the three pages above, PHP logs:

* <code>SaintapediaFeedback: wiki-config read failed for SaintapediaFeedbackNotifyUsersPage; using PHP value.</code> (and the same suffix for show-public-counts, enable-talklink)

Access/email/export no longer read a wiki page, so there's nothing to log a read failure for; a general cache outage still 500s the dashboard from <code>userCanManage()</code>.
